title: Sets of Real Numbers: Rational and Irrational
seo_title: Grade 8 Sets of Real Numbers Worksheets: Rational and Irrational (TEKS 8.2A, STAAR)
standard_text: 8.2A extend previous knowledge of sets and subsets using a visual representation to describe relationships between sets of real numbers
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 worksheets for Texas TEKS 8.2A: classify real numbers with a Venn diagram, rational and irrational numbers, repeating decimals and number set facts. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: √49 = 7 is rational; √50 and π are irrational.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • The real numbers are all the rational and irrational numbers.
  • Rational: can be written as a fraction of integers. Terminating and repeating decimals are rational, and so are perfect-square roots like √49 = 7.
  • Irrational: the decimal never ends and never repeats, such as π, √2 and √50.
  • Inside the rationals: integers ⊃ whole numbers ⊃ natural numbers.

Examples

Example

Classify √36.

√36 = 6

Answer: natural, whole, integer, rational, real

Example

Classify √20.

20 is not a perfect square

Answer: irrational, real

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Thinking every square root is irrational√49 = 7 is rational.
Thinking repeating decimals are irrational0.333… = 1/3 is rational.
Thinking π = 3.14 exactly3.14 is only an approximation; π is irrational.

faq.a: Extend previous knowledge of sets and subsets using a visual representation to describe relationships between sets of real numbers.

faq.q: Can a number be rational and irrational?
faq.a: No. Every real number is one or the other.

faq.q: How do I know if √n is rational?
faq.a: For a whole number n, √n is rational only if n is a perfect square.
